source_basis: This model progresses as such: the preliminary analysis serves to give an overview. Next, the agent-based model. Then, the differential equation model.
interpretation: Three-beat roadmap names overview, check, and fast stand-in before any equation.
applicability: Open a multi-model paper by giving the order and the job of each model.
counterevidence: The summary later restates the same three models, so the cadence is slightly redundant.

source_basis: exit signs simply point to the nearest exit as a heuristic guess for the best plan
interpretation: The baseline is labeled a guess, which keeps it from being read as the optimum.
applicability: Name a starting rule as a heuristic guess when a later section may replace it.
counterevidence: The recommendation never exhibits a better signing, so the guess remains the only concrete plan.

source_basis: the one congruity in this multi-faceted system is an exit plan
interpretation: Variety of emergencies is conceded, then collapsed to a single decision object.
applicability: Narrow a wide scenario list to the one object the model will touch.
counterevidence: Later sections show damage and delay do change the answer, so the congruity is a scope choice, not a fact.

source_basis: Indeed, the arrow and universal iconography of an exit sign is a common ground for the diverse crowd
interpretation: A control device is defended by who can read it and by surviving a power cut.
applicability: Justify a low-tech control by audience and by the failure it still works through.
counterevidence: Subject-verb agreement slips (is / are), a spoken-draft tell.

source_basis: These terms may appear interchangeably to refer to these elements.
interpretation: Aliases are declared so that room, node and site stay one variable.
applicability: When prose swaps everyday and graph words, say so once.
counterevidence: Congestion, bottleneckedness and viscosity are listed as aliases but later mean different things.

source_basis: We hand annotated a publicly available floor plan, and manually entered data about room size and connectivity
interpretation: The graph is homemade and the paper says so.
applicability: State hand entry instead of citing a dataset that does not exist.
counterevidence: No vertex count, no edge list, no reproducibility package.

source_basis: This situation is unrealistic since the shortest path to a target location may pass through heavily congested rooms.
interpretation: A graph-distance policy is rejected in the same paragraph that states it.
applicability: Kill a naive recommendation by naming the mechanism it ignores.
counterevidence: The rejection is qualitative; no congested shortest path is exhibited yet.

source_basis: lambda_2/2 <= Phi_G <= 2 sqrt(lambda_2), with lambda_2 = 0.009287497
interpretation: An intractable cut size is replaced by a cited inequality and a printed interval.
applicability: When the exact constant is too costly, bound it and print both ends.
counterevidence: The interval spans 0.0046 to 0.193, so the bound barely constrains the cut.

interpretation: The same interval is also written as a midpoint plus or minus half-width, which reads like a measurement.
applicability: Prefer the inequality over a plus-minus when the source is a bound.
counterevidence: The arithmetic of the half-width is consistent with the two endpoints.

source_basis: the partition severs only 4 corridors. One of these is the Richelieu entrance itself
interpretation: The spectral picture is cashed into a corridor count and a named wing.
applicability: After a Fiedler plot, say how many links the cut breaks and what they are.
counterevidence: The four corridors are not listed, only counted and located by wing.

source_basis: assuming that the designer of the building desired efficient egress, we can expect exits to be placed in locations that minimize the average path length
interpretation: A missing coordinate is replaced by an explicit design hypothesis.
applicability: Label imputed locations as guesses under a stated design goal.
counterevidence: No check against staff knowledge is possible from public data, and none is claimed.

source_basis: This model does not consider a number of salient realities. We address these issues with the subsequent model.
interpretation: The limitation list is the handoff, not an appendix apology.
applicability: End a model section by naming the gap the next model is for.
counterevidence: Grammar slips (This an algebraic) mark a draft sentence.

source_basis: Like we mentioned, while the connectivity model gives us useful insights, it doesn't take into consideration many other factors at play.
interpretation: Spoken callback credits the previous model and names the missing factor.
applicability: Open a successor model in the speaking voice rather than with a formalism.
counterevidence: doesn't is informal for a contest paper; it is also the voice.

source_basis: 2,532.83 people/hr for 2017. We estimate 3 hrs. Thus the average population is 7,598.49 people.
interpretation: A stock is a cited rate times an estimated dwell, printed to two decimals.
applicability: Show the product and mark which factor was estimated.
counterevidence: Two-decimal precision on an estimated dwell overstates the measurement.

source_basis: From queuing theory we know that given k events uniformly distributed in time, the time between events follows an Erlang distribution. k = 1 reduces to exponential.
interpretation: The distribution is imported from a named theory and then reduced in print.
applicability: Cite the distribution family and show the special case you actually sample.
counterevidence: The uniform-events premise is not checked against how visitors really move.

source_basis: the average time increases as congestion forms. Thus mu = t_0 * exp(c rho(u)). In other words, the more people, the harder it becomes to move.
interpretation: Prose says the mean time grows and movement gets harder, but if mu is a rate then exp(+c rho) makes transfers faster as density rises. The scalar ODE later uses exp(-c rho).
applicability: Check the sign of a state-dependent rate against the sentence under it.
counterevidence: If mu were a mean time rather than a rate, the sign would match the prose, but the exponential reduction treats mu as the Exp parameter.

source_basis: If we can we, move that person and they are not blocked, then we advance time. If not, we add another random number to their time.
interpretation: The event loop is narrated in speech order, including a stumble, with both branches present.
applicability: A spoken restatement of an algorithm helps when both branches stay visible.
counterevidence: The stumble makes the success condition grammatically ambiguous.

source_basis: the emergency personnel follow the same behaviors and interactions as normal evacuees, but have priority. c_s < c
interpretation: A second agent class is the same model with one inequality changed.
applicability: Add an agent class by naming the single parameter that differs.
counterevidence: Priority is also described as moving first, which is a queue rule, not only a smaller c.

source_basis: We guessed that seeking the target area in the middle of the evacuation will take the longest because that is when peak congestion occurs.
interpretation: A falsifiable sentence is placed before the bar chart.
applicability: Write the guess, then the figure, then whether the figure agreed.
counterevidence: The following paragraph reads peaks off the chart but never says the guess was confirmed or rejected in those words.

source_basis: for a museum population density of 0.3, congestion seems to be highest around 5 minutes. For 0.65, around 10 minutes.
interpretation: The crowded moment shifts later as density rises. seems marks a visual read.
applicability: Hedge a peak time that was read off averaged bars.
counterevidence: No trial count and no spread, so the minutes are not estimated times.

source_basis: it may be strategic for the emergency personnel to delay their appearance when the threat is not critical – typically with lower densities
interpretation: An exception to immediate entry is hedged and tied to low density.
applicability: Keep may when a chart suggests a delay but no optimizer was run.
counterevidence: The same paragraph says immediate response is ideal across densities, so the exception fights the main claim.

source_basis: could be modeled in aggregate as something similar to a viscous non-Newtonian fluid percolating through a porous substrate
interpretation: could and something similar to keep the fluid analogy from becoming an identity.
applicability: Hedge a physical analogy in the sentence that introduces it.
counterevidence: No fluid equation is then used; the analogy is motivational.

source_basis: One would imagine that museum-goers are stressed when evacuation but here we mean the force over area kind
interpretation: A footnote blocks the psychological reading of a mechanical word.
applicability: When a technical word has an everyday sense in the same paragraph, correct it in the open.
counterevidence: The footnote is grammatically unfinished, which softens the correction.

source_basis: d(rho)/dt = [A B(rho) + E] odot V^{-1} N(rho) - [A^T V^{-1} N(rho)] odot B(rho)
interpretation: Inflow and outflow are written with Hadamard products so blocking multiplies the receiving end.
applicability: A continuum evacuation on a directed graph needs an explicit blocking factor at capacity.
counterevidence: A, V and E are never filled in numerically.

source_basis: scalar flow already multiplies by exp(-c rho_u)/t_0, and n_i = (1/t_0) exp(-c rho_i) (3-2 rho_i) rho_i^2
interpretation: The exponential penalty appears in the scalar template and again inside n_i, so a vector step may apply it twice.
applicability: Check whether a named factor already contains the term written beside it.
counterevidence: The scalar display may be schematic and the vector form the one that is stepped.

source_basis: b_i = (1+2 rho_i)(1-rho_i)^2 and n_i carries rho_i^2
interpretation: Both polynomials hit the boundary values the prose promised: b(0)=1, b(1)=0, n(0)=0.
applicability: Give the polynomial when the prose only states the endpoint conditions.
counterevidence: n(1) is not 1, despite the prose saying n_u(1) = 1.

source_basis: The most trivial case is when some damage completely disallows visitors to exit. A more relevant situation occurs when disconnections still keep our floor plan a connected graph.
interpretation: A degenerate damage case is named and set aside before the connected case is modeled.
applicability: Say which scenario you refuse and why it is not a routing question.
counterevidence: Total cutoff is the more dangerous case, so calling it trivial is a modeling convenience.

source_basis: It's been said that something like 80% of people go to the Louvre just to see the Mona Lisa. Indeed, a visualization of Geo-tagged Instagram photos in 2014 shows a higher density.
interpretation: A folk percentage is hedged and a photo map is offered as the picture.
applicability: Keep it's been said on a borrowed percentage, and pair it with an independent picture.
counterevidence: Instagram geotags are not a visitor census.

source_basis: we don't see a significant difference when the distribution of persons is not uniform. Therefore it is reasonable to evaluate exit strategies without gathering the population per room.
interpretation: A null visual result is turned into permission to skip a dataset.
applicability: A factor that does not move the answer can justify a coarser input.
counterevidence: significant is not a reported test, and the nonuniform pattern is one hand-built reweighting of 15 rooms.

source_basis: It seems that crowd self-interaction combined with the time required to reverse exit sign direction has a compounding effect in higher densities.
interpretation: Two mechanisms are named for a sharp worsening, with it seems because they were not separated.
applicability: Name an interaction you did not factorialize, and keep the hedge.
counterevidence: No run isolates the reversal delay from the congestion penalty.

source_basis: This model is not effective at determining the evacuation time for a given plan. However, the analysis yielded some very key insights into the structure.
interpretation: Comparison refuses one job and assigns another instead of crowning a winner.
applicability: In a model-comparison section, give each model the question it can answer.
counterevidence: very key is filler; the content is the job split.

source_basis: could best be understood as a model of average behavior. However, we also found this model to be very hard to tune which prevented in depth analysis.
interpretation: A built model is assigned the role of an average and then confessed as unused.
applicability: Report a model you could not calibrate instead of dropping it silently.
counterevidence: No tuning attempt is shown, so the confession is unspecific.

source_basis: This might suggest a museum policy of breaking up large groups of tourists when
interpretation: The future-work sentence is cut off on the page.
applicability: Do not complete a truncated policy sentence and then cite it as a finding.
counterevidence: The intended ending is easy to guess, but it is not on the page.

source_basis: While we were unable to do much analysis on the differential flow model, but it has the potential to give key insights
interpretation: An unused tool is left on the table with the question it would have answered.
applicability: Admit an analysis was not done and still name the question.
counterevidence: The doubled while/but is a draft splice.

source_basis: a longer path might actually reduce congestion and hence counter-intuitively speed up egress
interpretation: The decision exception is the reason the bottleneck metric exists.
applicability: State the case where the locally worse choice improves the global time, and keep might.
counterevidence: No corridor is shown where the longer path won.

source_basis: we would suggest using a genetic algorithm or simulated annealing to determine whether or not a closest exit strategy needs modification
interpretation: The client is handed a search, not a fake optimized sign plan.
applicability: Recommend the computation when you did not run it, and keep whether or not.
counterevidence: Naming two optimizers without a representation of the signing is not yet a procedure.

source_basis: we advise the museum leaders to utilize it to determine the number of exits such that the evacuation time has an upper bound
interpretation: The delivered decision rule is a bound the client chooses, not a number of doors.
applicability: Hand over a model as an instrument plus the inequality the client should enforce.
counterevidence: The bound's value is never proposed.

source_basis: Graph representation of the Louvre. Colors indicate how far a room is from one of the four main exits.
interpretation: One color scale answers distance-to-exit on the hand-built graph.
applicability: Color a layout by the quantity the graph was built to show.
counterevidence: The in-figure title says Connections to nearest exit, which is a count, while the caption says how far, a distance.

source_basis: grouped bars of time to target against density, colored by response delay, averaged across trials
interpretation: A grouped bar chart is the right comparison: delay within density.
applicability: Use grouped bars when the question is which delay is slow at each density.
counterevidence: No error bars, so the average hides the stochastic spread the text itself flags.

source_basis: Time it takes to do a full evacuation, with different setups. Averaged across simulation trials
interpretation: The decision plot compares setups on one clock.
applicability: One axis, one outcome, several setups, and say the bars are averages.
counterevidence: Setups are not defined in the caption, so the figure does not stand alone.

source_basis: Chung on Cheeger inequalities beside Statista visitor counts, a New York Times piece, and a room-capacity how-to
interpretation: Authority is mixed on purpose: a theorem, an official series, journalism, a practical note.
applicability: A policy paper may cite all four, but should not give them equal weight in a numeric claim.
counterevidence: The 80 percent Mona Lisa line is journalism used next to the visitor series.

source_basis: maximum safe capacity of the Louvre, footprint 72,735 m^2, is 21,748 people based on safety code recommendations
interpretation: Capacity is a cited code applied to a footprint, not a measured count.
applicability: Say the code and the area when a cap is derived.
counterevidence: The code citation is a general how-to, not the French code for this building.

source_basis: We use Euler's method to approximate the solution at 1 second intervals. A room is at equilibrium if 0.1 < rho < 0.9.
interpretation: The integrator and the equilibrium label are both stated, and the label is a band rather than a fixed point.
applicability: Name the stepper and define the words you will use on the plot.
counterevidence: No step-size check is reported.

source_basis: Stochastic outcomes may necessitate multiple simulations to get a good sense of average-case behavior.
interpretation: The paper itself says one agent run is not a result.
applicability: Repeat a stochastic evacuation and say you did.
counterevidence: The trial count is never given, so the advice is not followed in print.
